frontend.prompt:
Implement client-side edit behavior for the entry.description field with explicit dirty tracking and three-way semantics (absent / null / string) as follows:

1) State and user interactions
- Load the current description from the server and keep an originalDescription value.
- Track a descriptionDirty flag that is set to true only when the user explicitly modifies the description field (typing, deleting, or using an explicit "Clear" action). Do not set descriptionDirty just because the form was opened.
- Provide an explicit "Clear" action in the UI. When the user uses Clear, set an internal descriptionOutgoingValue marker to null and set descriptionDirty = true.
- When the user edits (types or deletes) the text field, set descriptionOutgoingValue to the current text (which may be the empty string) and descriptionDirty = true.

2) Submit behavior (PUT)
- On PUT, include the description key in the JSON body only when descriptionDirty == true. If descriptionDirty == false, omit the description key entirely so the server sees it as absent and will not change the stored value.
- If descriptionDirty == true and the user used Clear, include "description": null in the JSON body.
- If descriptionDirty == true and the user edited the field to an empty string, include "description": "" (empty string) in the JSON body.
- If descriptionDirty == true and the user edited to a non-empty string, include that string value.
- Preserve the existing request format and other fields of the PUT body; do not change payload envelope or HTTP method used by other parts of the client.

3) Validation
- For any non-null string value to be sent, enforce client-side validation that the string length <= 255. If validation fails, block the submit and show a validation error message. Do not silently truncate server-bound data.
- Do not convert absent values into null before sending. Do not convert empty strings into null. Treat null, empty string, and absent as distinct.

4) Tests / acceptance checks (client-side)
- Unit/integration tests that assert the three PUT behaviors:
  a) Unchanged description: open edit form and submit without changing description -> request body must omit description key.
  b) Clear: use explicit Clear action -> request body must include "description": null.
  c) Empty string: delete all characters in the field (marking it dirty) -> request body must include "description": "".
  d) Non-empty: edit to new value -> request body includes the new string.
  e) Length enforcement: attempt to send >255 characters -> client blocks submit and shows validation error.

5) Non-goals / constraints
- Do not change creation (POST) behavior for description; creation rules remain as before.
- Do not change server API contract or error formats; conform to existing request/response conventions when reporting validation errors.

backend.prompt:
Change the PUT/update handler for entries so the server distinguishes between three cases for description: absent (do not modify), present null (set DB NULL), present string (including empty string). Implement the following.

1) Request parsing and presence detection
- When parsing the PUT JSON body, detect whether the description key is present in the request object (key presence), not merely whether its value is truthy/defined.
- Treat three distinct states:
  a) Key absent: caller did not include description in the payload -> do not modify the description column in the database.
  b) Key present with value null: caller explicitly requests clearing -> set description column to NULL.
  c) Key present with a string value (including the empty string): update description to that exact string.

2) Validation
- For any non-null string provided, validate length <= 255. If length > 255, reject the update with a validation error consistent with existing API conventions (do not silently truncate). Do not invent a new error format; follow existing error-handling patterns.
- Do not coerce empty strings into NULLs.

3) Update semantics / DB operation
- Build the UPDATE operation so it only sets description when the request explicitly provides it. Concretely:
  - If key absent: exclude description from the SET clause.
  - If key present: include description = <value> in the SET clause where <value> is either NULL or the provided string.
- If using an ORM, use a patch/partial-update API that only writes fields that are explicitly present in the incoming payload; avoid any update that overwrites unspecified fields with defaults or nulls.

4) Tests / acceptance checks (server-side)
- Unit/integration tests covering:
  a) Key absent: send PUT without description -> DB description remains unchanged.
  b) Key present null: send PUT with description: null -> DB description becomes SQL NULL.
  c) Key present empty string: send PUT with description: "" -> DB description becomes an empty string (not NULL).
  d) Key present long string >255 -> request rejected with validation error; DB unchanged.

5) Non-goals / constraints
- Do not change creation (POST) behavior for description; creation rules remain as-is.
- Do not transform absent into null or empty strings into null anywhere in the request processing pipeline.
- Keep error response style consistent with existing endpoints.
